events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon; Blue Mountains of Washington
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...WIDESPREAD BREEZY WESTERLY WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY
TODAY...

...HIGH-BASED SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS THROUGH THIS AFTERNOON
ALONG THE WASHINGTON CASCADES AND BLUE MOUNTAINS...

.An approaching low-pressure system will bring widespread breezy
westerly winds through the Cascade gaps, across the Columbia
Basin, and into portions of the Blue Mountains today. Coupled
with low relative humidity, this will lead to critical fire
weather conditions. Moreover, high-based showers and thunderstorms
are forecast, with the best chances of abundant lightning
through the remainder of this morning along the Washington
Cascades and this afternoon for the northeast Blue Mountains.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 692 Northern Blue Mountains
of Oregon and 692 Blue Mountains of Washington.

* TIMING...From 11 AM this morning to 11 PM PDT this evening.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Isolated to scattered coverage with abundant
lightning.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusty, erratic winds of 40 to 60 mph.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Kivalina and Red Dog Dock; Baldwin Peninsula; Shishmaref; Bering Strait Coast; Southern Seward Peninsula Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
A Bering Sea low will move into the Gulf of Anadyr then the
Chukchi Sea on Monday. South-southwest winds will increase water
levels to around 1 to 3 feet above the normal high tide line
during the Monday and Tuesday high tides in the Seward Peninsula.
Water levels around 2 to 4 feet above the normal high tide line
are possible from Kotzebue to Kivalina. There is still quite a bit
of uncertainty with the exact water level heights and they will
be monitored over the next few days.

events.region: Western Arctic Coast; Northwest Arctic Coast; Northern Arctic Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
A Bering Sea low will move into the Gulf of Anadyr then the
Chukchi Sea on Monday. South-southwest winds will increase water
levels to around 1 to 3 feet above the normal high tide line
during the Monday and Tuesday high tides from Wainwright to
Utqiagvik. Water levels around 2 to 4 feet above the normal high
tide line are possible from Point Lay to Point Hope. Secondly,
winds will shift west-northwest Tuesday afternoon which can
prolong high water levels into Wednesday. There is still quite a
bit of uncertainty with the exact water level heights and they
will be monitored over the next few days.
